newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Kuchma proposes council for Ukraine reform moves.
newsitem.headline: Kuchma proposes council for Ukraine reform moves.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma proposed on Wednesday setting up a presidential council to take important economic decisions, possibly including approval of the budget.

Kuchma's proposal, outlined in a letter to parliament, responded to the chamber delaying approval of this year's budget by six months -- a move which threatened an International Monetary Fund (IMF) loan.
"I think it would be expedient to create a joint council with representatives of the president and parliament," Kuchma wrote.
He did not rule out that the council or the president might be given the right to approve the budget.

Kuchma also reiterated that he was considering proposing a constitutional change to postpone the next parliamentary election, due in March 1998, by one year. The move is intended to allow more time for economic reforms to be passed.
"I think that with deputies' approval, the term of the Supreme Council (parliament) could be extended to five years by amending Ukraine's constitution," Kuchma wrote.
Parliament passed this year's budget only on June 27. The delay held up a $2.5-$3 billion loan from the IMF and dented the trust of some foreign investors already worried by corruption.

Kuchma responded by saying parliament's term could be extended by one year to give them more time to pass economic reforms. But deputies said such a move would violate the constitution, which says parliament is elected for four years.

The IMF mission in Kiev was not immediately available for comment. Its chief representative in Ukraine has said the Fund might issue a smaller, interim stand-by loan if its wish list of 41 conditions is not complete by July 18.
